rule: Every idea is judged on the design period (2019 to mid-2024) first. Only ideas that work there are adopted; the hold-out (mid-2024 onward) is a check, never a reason to adopt. IC = rank correlation with the next 20 trading days' returns (0.05+ is useful on NEPSE).

items.note: The core of model v3.

items.idea: True market capitalisation instead of turnover
items.note: Weaker than turnover and reversed on unseen data. Crowding, not size, is what matters.
Key insight: most of the crowd edge comes from avoiding crowded SECTORS (the big banks). That is why the model lagged in 2025–26, when banks led.
Worked only on unseen data; adopting it now would be curve-fitting. Re-tested as data grows.

items.idea: Dividend payers, cash yield, bonus history
items.note: Strong in 2024–26 only, a possible regime shift towards quality. Not adopted on hold-out evidence alone.
Same story: a 2024–26 effect that did not exist before.
No effect.

items.idea: Machine learning (gradient boosting, ridge) on 26 signals, walk-forward
items.note: The simple fixed-weight score beat both models. About 200 tradable stocks is too little data for complex models; they learn noise.
Chasing recent signal performance added noise and a deeper worst drop.
Stopped-out stocks did not keep falling; stops locked in losses and doubled trading.

items.idea: Market timing (index trend / bear-market cash filter)
items.note: Cost return without reducing the worst drop.

items.idea: Count cash dividends (after 5% tax) on book-closure dates
items.note: Real money investors receive. NEPSE's index excludes dividends, so the bot now has a ~1–2%/yr structural advantage in comparisons.
Results survive doubled costs.

items.idea: Bootstrap 90% ranges for the yearly edge
items.holdout: vs NEPSE ≈0 (−7 to +16); vs avg stock +4.5 to +5.6 (−1 to +15)
items.note: Stock selection very likely adds value (~93% chance vs the average stock); beating the cap-weighted NEPSE index is a coin flip.

items.idea: How fragile is the Rs 1 lakh (10-stock) portfolio?
items.holdout: +19% to +45% depending on start date / a single different pick
items.note: With only 10 stocks, one different pick in 2021 changed the 2024–26 result by 16 points. The 16-stock Rs 5 lakh portfolio stays within +33% to +37%. More stocks = less luck; add capital and positions when you can.
Chasing spikes reliably loses. See Quick trades.
Priced in before it is public.

items.idea: Classic chart signals and checklist (2–3 weeks)
items.note: Same as random. Kept as an experiment with a live scoreboard.
Only today's sheet is published; saved daily since 2026-11-25. Testable in 6–12 months, or now if NepseAlpha's history can be exported.

items.idea: Quarterly fundamentals (EPS, P/E, P/B, ROE, NPL, bank rates)
items.note: Only the latest quarter is published; point-in-time snapshots saved weekly since 2026-11-26 (266 companies). Enables value, quality and earnings-surprise tests later.
ShareSansar's rate feed errors. Bank base rates and cost of funds are now collected from quarterly reports as a substitute; NRB monthly data would need a manual download.
Not archived publicly, so cannot be backtested.
